course_position.stage_name: Solid B1+ to Low B2 Development

lesson_intent.one_sentence_goal: Give a longer spoken explanation with one reason, one condition, and one exception.
lesson_intent.real_life_context: Explaining a schedule conflict clearly enough that another person can act on it.
lesson_intent.communicative_function: Organizing a short explanation across several turns without losing word order.

dialogue_task.scenario: Anna and Erik prepare a clear explanation for why a shared plan needs to change and what can still work.

main_focus.name: combining reason, condition, and exception clauses
main_focus.description: Combine eftersom, om, and trots att in a controlled explanation where each clause has a clear job.
model_examples: Vi behöver ändra planen eftersom tiden krockar.
Om du kan komma senare, fungerar det trots att mötet blir långt.
main_focus.desired_presence: Use 4-6 subordinate clauses total, but avoid more than two clauses in a single sentence.

avoid_grammar: three-clause chains that are hard to follow
passive constructions as the main pattern

useful_chunks: Trots att det blir lite sent...
vocabulary_target.desired_presence: Prioritize chunks that help the learner produce a clear multi-turn explanation.

dialogue_shape.opening: A practical misunderstanding or unclear plan creates a need for a better explanation.
dialogue_shape.middle: They rebuild the explanation using a reason, a condition, and one exception.
dialogue_shape.ending: They agree on a clear version of the plan that could be sent or said to someone else.

target_complexity.repetition: Recycle the week naturally, with clarity more important than adding extra grammar.

focus: the main reason behind the changed plan
the condition that would make the plan work
the exception or obstacle that must still be considered

sentence_focus: one sentence introducing the reason with anledningen är att
one sentence with om and a possible solution
one sentence with trots att and an obstacle
one sentence summarizing the clarified plan
